added_failures_note: The reviewed run recorded no baseline_suite and no after_suite (both null in its manifest), so it carries no two-arm suite delta of its own and the added-failure set is empty rather than measured by a suite that could have exercised it. Its gate was the per-arm runner docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab-run.py, whose log runner-heuristic.log ends EXIT=0; the change touches only docs/evidence paths that no test module covers.

1.reason: the landing contract names each fragment by its node id

findings.text: follow-on: the landing fragment reports only the three documentation scores after harmonization and omits that the apply halted after batch 1 of 2 and that the anchor member's score fell from 1.0 to 0.849 -- precisely the lower-score condition the section's adoption rule turns on; the record carries both (scores_before, score_regressions and halt_reasons), but the landing prose reads as a neutral completion and a reader of the fragment alone cannot see that this arm worsened its own anchor.

follow-on: the landing filename and its section id embed the plan abbreviation ssog and a -r2 version marker, both of which the naming rules forbid in a path, so the fragment cannot be understood apart from the plan; the pattern is mandated verbatim by the sprint's working rules, so the defect is the convention's rather than the worker's, and prior siblings in this sprint were flagged the same way.

follow-on: the harmonize receipt's member_scores records the anchor member at 1.0, its pre-apply value, while the same record's scores_after (line 219) records it at 0.849, so two similarly named fields carry opposing values for the same member; a consumer that reads member_scores rather than scores_after would miss the score fall the section's rule is designed to catch, and the record documents neither field's time-base.

justifications.durability: the diff adds no assertion at all -- it is a data record and a doc -- so nothing committed reddens if the record's scores or containment verdict were later replaced, and the only guard is the runner's write-time containment gate, exercised through --self-check-containment rather than through a test of this change.
justifications.evidence: the gate is the arm invocation whose log runner-heuristic.log ends EXIT=0 with the summary line "lint 0->0, 73 calls, $1.2403, 1654.1s, stamped=False, containment=True", the record's numbers reconcile with the apply log's own receipt (cost_spent reconciles at 1.240277), and the containment guard's refusal was demonstrated on this record by --self-check-containment (4 cases, 3 planted-live cases fail as expected) although that control belongs to the unchanged runner.
justifications.fit: the record reproduces the sibling arm schema key for key and the HTML follows the evidence-fragment idiom, but the landing filename carries the plan abbreviation ssog and a -r2 version marker, and the receipt keeps the runner's member_scores (pre-apply) beside scores_after (post-apply), two similarly named fields that diverge whenever a member's score moves.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab/momentum_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift-heuristic.json:175 records the arm at outcome_status complete with the fixed anchor, and its isolation block proves the apply wrote to a scratch copy (scratch_probe 1, live_probe 0) rather than the live graph.
justifications.reuse: the change adds no new definition and forks no capability the repository owns -- the record is produced by the existing runner docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab-run.py and the fragment reuses the existing plan-fragment shape.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff -- the arm JSON and the landing fragment ssog-anchor-exb-momentum-heuristic-r2.html -- is inside the three declared write paths, and the earlier attempt's files were left in place rather than overwritten in a second path.
